entries.title: Newborn Male Circumcision (Elective Procedure Counselling)

entries.title: Approach to Congenital Heart Disease (Epidemiology, Cyanotic vs. Acyanotic Classification, Initial Investigations)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 62 (Abnormal heart sounds and murmurs) requires differentiating innocent from pathologic murmurs/heart sounds as an entry point to diagnosing CHD, which is this unit's classification-framework content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: the cyanotic-vs-acyanotic physiologic framework this unit teaches is the direct diagnostic scaffold for objective 19 (Cyanosis and hypoxia) applied to a pediatric/neonatal cause.

testable_competencies.classification: Apply the cyanotic-vs-acyanotic (L-to-R shunt/obstruction beyond lungs vs. R-to-L shunt/mixing) physiologic framework and initial investigations (echo, ECG, CXR, pre-/post-ductal saturations, 4-limb BPs, hyperoxia test) to a newly suspected congenital heart lesion.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: VSD is the most common CHD lesion and its classic finding (holosystolic murmur at LLSB, murmur intensity inversely related to defect size) is the paradigm teaching case for objective 62.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize VSD by size-dependent clinical course (small VSD: asymptomatic, spontaneous closure; moderate-to-large VSD: CHF by 2 mo, holosystolic murmur at LLSB with mid-diastolic apical rumble, risk of late pulmonary hypertension if untreated) and the indication for surgical closure by 1 yr in large defects.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: ASD's classic exam finding (wide, fixed split S2 with a pulmonic outflow murmur) is a paradigm teaching case for objective 62.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize the three ASD subtypes (ostium primum -- associated with Down syndrome; ostium secundum -- most common; sinus venosus), the fixed-split-S2 exam finding, and the high spontaneous-closure rate for small defects vs. elective closure for larger ones.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: the continuous 'machinery' murmur of PDA best heard at the left infraclavicular area is a paradigm teaching case for objective 62.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize PDA's association with prematurity, the continuous machinery murmur with bounding pulses/wide pulse pressure, and that indomethacin (prostaglandin-E2 antagonist) is effective only in premature infants, with catheter/surgical closure reserved for term infants or persistent/complicated PDA.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypertension/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 9-1 (Hypertension) applies directly -- coarctation's classic finding is a blood-pressure discrepancy between upper and lower extremities (brachial-femoral delay), a key secondary-hypertension cause in children.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: the late-peaking systolic murmur at the apex/left axilla/left back is a secondary teaching point for objective 62.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize coarctation by blood-pressure discrepancy between upper and lower extremities (brachial-femoral delay, >20 mmHg difference raising suspicion), its association with bicuspid aortic valve and Turner syndrome, and that severe neonatal presentation is a ductal-dependent emergency requiring prostaglandin E1 to keep the ductus open.

entries.title: Aortic Stenosis and Pulmonary Stenosis (Valvular Obstructive Lesions)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct-component match: the systolic ejection murmur at the RUSB (aortic) or LUSB (pulmonary) with an ejection click is a paradigm teaching case for objective 62's innocent-vs-pathologic murmur differentiation.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize valvular vs. subvalvular/supravalvular aortic and pulmonary stenosis by exam findings (systolic ejection murmur with ejection click for valvular disease) and that severe neonatal obstructive lesions present as duct-dependent circulatory collapse when the ductus closes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: Tetralogy of Fallot is the most common cyanotic CHD lesion and the classic teaching case for objective 19 (Cyanosis and hypoxia) in a neonate/infant, including the 'boot-shaped heart' CXR finding and hypercyanotic ('tet') spells.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize Tetralogy of Fallot's four components (VSD, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, overriding aorta, RVH), boot-shaped heart on CXR, and hypercyanotic spell management (knee-to-chest positioning, oxygen, morphine, fluids).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: TGA is a ductal-dependent cyanotic lesion presenting with severe hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen at ductal closure -- a paradigm teaching case for objective 19, with the classic 'egg-shaped heart' CXR finding.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize TGA's ductal-dependent physiology (progressive hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen as the ductus closes), egg-shaped-heart CXR sign, and the emergency management sequence (prostaglandin E1 to maintain ductal patency, balloon atrial septostomy, definitive arterial switch surgery).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: TAPVR is a less common cyanotic lesion (1-2% of CHD) relevant to objective 19's differential but with lower expected question-coverage weight than the higher-yield lesions above, given the 'snowman heart' CXR sign is a classic but lower-frequency recall item.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize TAPVR's pathophysiology (all pulmonary veins drain to the right-sided circulation; an ASD is obligatory for survival) and the classic 'snowman' heart silhouette on CXR.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: a less common cyanotic lesion relevant to objective 19's differential.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize truncus arteriosus's pathophysiology (single great vessel gives rise to the aorta, pulmonary, and coronary arteries, overlying a large VSD) and the need for surgical repair within the first 6 wk of life.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: HLHS is the most common cause of death from CHD in the first month of life and a paradigm ductal-dependent-systemic-circulation emergency for objective 19 -- circulatory shock/metabolic acidosis on ductal closure is a classic, high-stakes teaching point.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize HLHS as ductal-dependent for systemic circulation (shock and metabolic acidosis on ductal closure), and the emergency management sequence (intubation, metabolic-acidosis correction, IV prostaglandin E1 to maintain ductal patency, surgical palliation or transplant).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: a less common cyanotic lesion relevant to objective 19's differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/genetic-concerns/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Weak/indirect match: teratogenic association (maternal lithium/benzodiazepine exposure) touches on objective 36 (Genetic concerns)'s prenatal-risk-factor scope, but this is not a primary genetic-counselling teaching point in the source text.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize Ebstein's anomaly (apically displaced, malformed tricuspid valve leaflets), its association with maternal lithium/benzodiazepine exposure and with accessory conduction pathways (e.g. WPW).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: CHF is frequently first recognized through an abnormal heart sound/gallop rhythm or murmur, linking to objective 62.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pediatric CHF by age-specific presentation (infant: poor feeding, diaphoresis with feeds, FTT; older child: exercise intolerance, recurrent 'URTIs'/'asthma') and the 4 key exam features (tachycardia, tachypnea, cardiomegaly, hepatomegaly), and identify the underlying CHD or other cause.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Explicitly cross-referenced by the source text to the adult Cardiology chapter (C40) for general CHF pathophysiology/management; primary ownership not finalized at this scope stage per the pending global cross-discipline audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/syncope-and-pre-syncope/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: pediatric dysrhythmias (most commonly SVT) present with objective 106 (Syncope and pre-syncope) or palpitation-type symptoms in the age-appropriate differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize supraventricular tachycardia as the most common pediatric dysrhythmia (narrow-complex, rate typically >220 bpm in infants) and the initial management sequence (vagal maneuvers, adenosine, synchronized cardioversion if unstable).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-heart-sounds-and-murmurs/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 62 'Abnormal heart sounds and murmurs' explicitly requires differentiating innocent from pathologic conditions -- the paradigm objective for this unit.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Differentiate innocent/functional pediatric murmurs (soft, systolic, no associated symptoms, normal exam otherwise) from pathologic murmurs (diastolic, holosystolic, harsh/loud, associated with symptoms or abnormal exam findings) using history and physical exam features.

entries.title: Infective Endocarditis (Pediatric)

testable_competencies.risk_recognition: Recognize congenital heart disease (especially with prosthetic material or unrepaired cyanotic lesions) as the key pediatric risk factor for infective endocarditis and the indication for antibiotic prophylaxis before high-risk procedures.

entries.cross_discipline_note: The general infective-endocarditis competency is already represented by SU-C-30 and SU-ID-08 under objective 62; this unit retains the pediatric congenital-heart-disease and prophylaxis context. PRIMARY_OWNER is not finalized here.

entries.title: Global Developmental Delay

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/developmental-delay/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 21 'Developmental delay' is the paradigm objective, explicitly requiring use of a validated developmental screening tool and referral to early intervention services.

testable_competencies.screening_and_referral: Use a validated developmental screening tool to identify delay across two or more domains (global developmental delay), and refer for early developmental intervention services prior to formal subspecialty assessment.

entries.uncertain_reason: No dedicated MCC 'infective endocarditis' presentation-level objective exists in the registry (search-mcc-objectives found no direct match); pediatric IE risk is contextually relevant to fever-source and cardiac-complication reasoning but could not be confidently mapped.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/developmental-delay/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: intellectual disability is the older-child diagnostic outcome that global developmental delay (objective 21) may evolve into once formal cognitive testing is possible; not itself an MCC-named presentation.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize intellectual disability as significant limitation in both intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour with onset before 18 yr, distinct from isolated learning disorder.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/language-and-speech-disorders/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 44 'Language and speech disorders' is the paradigm objective, requiring differentiation of language from speech disorders.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Differentiate expressive/receptive language delay from isolated speech-sound (articulation) disorder, and recognize red flags (regression, no words by 18 mo, no phrases by 2 yr) warranting audiology and formal assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/attention-learning-and-school-problems/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 5 'Attention, learning, and school problems' explicitly covers assessment for causal/co-occurring conditions in a child with school difficulties, of which specific learning disorder (e.g. dyslexia) is a core cause.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize specific learning disorder as a discrepancy between academic achievement and cognitive potential in a specific domain (reading, writing, math) despite adequate instruction, and the role of interdisciplinary educational assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/genetic-concerns/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 36 (Genetic concerns) covers diagnosis of a condition with in-utero teratogenic causation; FASD's dysmorphic-features/growth-restriction/neurodevelopmental triad fits this scope, though FASD is a teratogenic rather than strictly genetic condition.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/developmental-delay/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: FASD is a leading preventable cause of developmental delay/intellectual disability, linking to objective 21.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the FASD diagnostic triad (characteristic facial features, growth restriction, CNS/neurodevelopmental abnormalities) and its basis in prenatal alcohol exposure.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 21 explicitly names autism spectrum disorders among causal conditions and directs developmental screening, early-intervention referral, and specialized or multidisciplinary assessment.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize core features of autism spectrum disorder (persistent deficits in social communication/interaction, restricted/repetitive behaviours and interests) and the role of early screening and referral for intensive behavioural intervention.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/attention-learning-and-school-problems/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 5 'Attention, learning, and school problems' is the paradigm objective for ADHD, explicitly noting frequent co-occurring conditions and the need for early interdisciplinary involvement.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Apply DSM-5 inattentive/hyperactive-impulsive criteria (symptoms in 2+ settings, onset before age 12) to diagnose ADHD, recognize common comorbidities (learning disorder, anxiety, ODD), and outline first-line management (behavioural strategies +/- stimulant medication).

entries.title: Motor Delay

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/developmental-delay/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: isolated motor delay is one domain assessed under objective 21's developmental screening scope; overlaps with the Hypotonia study unit (P.S15.T03) in the Neurology section when motor delay is due to central/peripheral hypotonia.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize motor-milestone red flags (not sitting by 9 mo, not walking by 18 mo) warranting further neurologic/developmental workup, distinguishing isolated motor delay from global developmental delay.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with the Hypotonia study unit (P.S15.T03); primary ownership not finalized at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/sodium-concentration-abnormal-serum/hypernatremia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: SIADH is a major cause of objective 99-1 (Hyponatremia) in the pediatric population.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/sodium-concentration-abnormal-serum/hyponatremia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: central/nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is a cause of objective 99-2 (Hypernatremia), particularly in a child with polyuria/polydipsia.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Differentiate SIADH (euvolemic hyponatremia, concentrated urine) from diabetes insipidus (polyuria, dilute urine despite hypernatremia/dehydration) and recognize their respective common pediatric causes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypoglycemia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 129 (Hypoglycemia) applies directly to insulin-treated pediatric T1DM and DKA-treatment complications.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hyperglycemia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 130 (Hyperglycemia) applies directly to new-onset diabetes/DKA presentation in children.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_management: Recognize new-onset pediatric T1DM (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss, DKA as a presenting emergency) versus T2DM (obesity-associated, often milder presentation), and outline initial DKA management principles (fluid resuscitation, insulin, electrolyte monitoring) and hypoglycemia recognition/treatment in an insulin-treated child.

entries.title: Growth Disorders (Short Stature, Growth Hormone Deficiency)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/stature-abnormal-tall-stature-short-stature/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 101 'Stature abnormal (tall stature / short stature)' is the paradigm objective for this unit's growth-disorder differential (familial short stature, constitutional delay of growth and puberty, growth hormone deficiency, and organic/chronic-disease causes).

testable_competencies.approach: Use growth-velocity trends and bone age to differentiate normal variants (familial short stature, constitutional delay of growth and puberty) from pathologic short stature (growth hormone deficiency, hypothyroidism, chronic disease, Turner syndrome) warranting endocrine referral.

entries.title: Disorders of Calcium Homeostasis (Hypercalcemia, Hypocalcemia, Rickets)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/calcium-disorders/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct-component match: objective 12-2 'Calcium disorders' is the paradigm objective for hyper-/hypocalcemia; rickets is the pediatric-specific manifestation of chronic hypocalcemia/vitamin D deficiency affecting the growth plate.

testable_competencies.approach: Use the PTH/vitamin D axis to work up hyper- and hypocalcemia, and recognize rickets (bowing deformity, widened wrists/costochondral junctions, delayed fontanelle closure) as the pediatric skeletal manifestation of chronic vitamin D deficiency or renal osteodystrophy.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neck-mass-goiter-thyroid-disease/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 63 (Neck masses and thyroid disease) covers thyroid disease diagnosis generally, of which pediatric-specific presentations (congenital hypothyroidism on newborn screen, autoimmune/Graves disease) are a subset.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/stature-abnormal-tall-stature-short-stature/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Weak/indirect match: untreated congenital hypothyroidism causes growth failure/short stature (objective 101), but this is a secondary rather than primary teaching link.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize congenital hypothyroidism as a newborn-screening priority (irreversible intellectual disability if treatment delayed) and distinguish it from acquired autoimmune hypothyroidism/Graves disease presenting later in childhood.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/congenital-anomalies-dysmorphic-features/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 36-2 (Congenital anomalies, dysmorphic features) covers the diagnostic approach to ambiguous genitalia/atypical genital development as a congenital anomaly requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abnormal-pubertal-development/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Weak/indirect match: DSD overlaps with objective 93-1 (Abnormal pubertal development) when it presents at puberty rather than in the newborn period, but the newborn-period ambiguous-genitalia presentation is this unit's primary content.

testable_competencies.approach: Recognize ambiguous genitalia in a newborn as a diagnostic and psychosocial emergency requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation (karyotype, hormone panel, imaging) before sex assignment, and understand the broad DSD classification (46,XX DSD; 46,XY DSD; sex chromosome DSD).

entries.title: Approach to the Infant/Child with Dehydration

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 22-3 'Pediatric diarrhea' explicitly requires attention to signs/symptoms of dehydration, hypovolemia, and electrolyte abnormalities, which is this unit's core content applied across all dehydration etiologies, not diarrhea alone.

testable_competencies.assessment_and_management: Clinically classify dehydration severity (mild/moderate/severe) using history and exam findings (capillary refill, mucous membranes, skin turgor, urine output, mental status) and select oral rehydration therapy vs. IV fluid resuscitation accordingly.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/vomiting-and-or-nausea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 116 'Vomiting and/or nausea' explicitly notes important causes arise outside the GI system (e.g. raised ICP, metabolic disease), directly applicable to the pediatric bilious-vs-nonbilious/age-based vomiting differential.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Distinguish bilious from non-bilious vomiting (bilious vomiting in a neonate/infant is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise -- malrotation with volvulus) and recognize non-GI causes (raised ICP, metabolic disease, UTI, pyloric stenosis).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/vomiting-and-or-nausea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: physiologic infant GER (effortless spitting up, 'happy spitter') is a common, usually benign cause within objective 116's vomiting differential, distinguished from pathologic GERD with FTT/esophagitis.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Distinguish physiologic GER ('happy spitter', normal growth) from pathologic GERD (FTT, esophagitis, respiratory complications) requiring further workup/treatment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 64 (Neonatal distress) covers assessment/stabilization of a distressed neonate; TEF is a classic structural cause presenting with choking/cyanosis with feeds and inability to pass an NG tube.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize TEF/esophageal atresia by inability to pass an NG tube, choking/cyanosis/coughing with first feeds, and polyhydramnios antenatally; recognize the VACTERL association.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/vomiting-and-or-nausea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: pyloric stenosis is a paradigm cause of objective 116's vomiting differential in a 2-8 wk old infant (projectile, non-bilious vomiting, hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, olive-shaped mass, target sign on ultrasound).

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize pyloric stenosis (projectile non-bilious vomiting in a 2-8 wk old, palpable olive-shaped mass, hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis) and the management sequence (fluid/electrolyte correction before pyloromyotomy).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/vomiting-and-or-nausea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: duodenal atresia is a cause of bilious vomiting in the newborn within objective 116's differential, classically with the 'double bubble' sign on abdominal X-ray and association with Down syndrome.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize duodenal atresia by the 'double bubble' sign on abdominal X-ray, bilious vomiting in the first day of life, and its association with Down syndrome.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/vomiting-and-or-nausea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: malrotation with midgut volvulus is the classic surgical emergency underlying objective 116's teaching point that bilious vomiting in an infant requires urgent evaluation.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize bilious vomiting +/- abdominal distension/pain/hematochezia in an infant as malrotation with volvulus until proven otherwise, requiring emergent upper GI contrast study and surgical consultation to prevent bowel ischemia.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 22-3 'Pediatric diarrhea' is the paradigm objective, requiring a detailed history and attention to dehydration/hypovolemia/electrolyte signs.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/acute-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 22-1 (Acute diarrhea, <1 wk) is the general adult-oriented parallel objective this pediatric-specific unit specializes.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/chronic-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 22-2 (Chronic diarrhea) is the general adult-oriented parallel objective for the chronic-diarrhea arm of this unit.

testable_competencies.approach: Classify pediatric diarrhea as acute (usually infectious/self-limited) vs. chronic (osmotic, secretory, inflammatory, or motility causes) and assess for dehydration as the primary complication to manage.

entries.title: Gastroenteritis (Pediatric, GI Chapter)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 22-3 'Pediatric diarrhea' applies directly to acute infectious gastroenteritis, the most common cause of acute pediatric diarrhea.

testable_competencies.management: Manage acute pediatric gastroenteritis with oral rehydration therapy as first-line treatment, recognize indications for IV fluids, and counsel on the self-limited course of most viral gastroenteritis (rotavirus, norovirus).

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with the Infectious Diseases section's 'Gastroenteritis' unit (P.S12.T04), which is pathogen-focused; this GI-chapter unit is fluid-management/clinical-course focused. Primary ownership not finalized at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: a benign, common cause of chronic pediatric diarrhea within objective 22-3's differential in an otherwise well, thriving toddler.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize toddler's diarrhea as a diagnosis of exclusion (chronic non-bloody diarrhea with undigested food particles in an otherwise well, normally-growing toddler, often related to excess fruit-juice intake), not requiring extensive workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: a cause of chronic osmotic diarrhea within objective 22-3's differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lactose intolerance (bloating, cramping, osmotic diarrhea temporally related to dairy intake) and distinguish primary/genetic from secondary/post-infectious lactase deficiency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abdominal-pain/chronic-abdominal-pain/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 3-3 (Chronic abdominal pain) covers the diagnostic approach IBS falls under as a functional GI disorder diagnosed by Rome IV criteria after red flags are excluded.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose pediatric IBS using Rome IV criteria after excluding organic red flags (weight loss, GI bleeding, nocturnal symptoms, family history of IBD/celiac).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: celiac disease is a key organic cause of chronic pediatric diarrhea/malabsorption within objective 22-3's differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/failure-to-thrive-infant-child/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: celiac disease is a recognized cause of failure to thrive (objective 31-2) when malabsorption is significant.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize celiac disease presentations (chronic diarrhea, FTT, abdominal distension, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis) and the diagnostic approach (tTG-IgA serology while on a gluten-containing diet, duodenal biopsy confirmation).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/allergic-reactions-and-atopy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 4 (Allergic reactions and atopy) covers food-allergy diagnosis generally; cow's milk protein allergy is the most common infant food allergy, presenting with GI symptoms +/- eczema/hematochezia.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cow's milk protein allergy (regurgitation, eczema, hematochezia, FTT in a formula- or breast-fed infant) and first-line management (extensively hydrolyzed or amino-acid formula, or maternal dairy elimination if breastfeeding).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: pediatric-onset IBD is an important organic cause of chronic diarrhea within objective 22-3's differential.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/failure-to-thrive-infant-child/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: growth failure/FTT (objective 31-2) is a hallmark of pediatric Crohn disease, sometimes preceding overt GI symptoms.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pediatric IBD (chronic diarrhea +/- blood/mucus, abdominal pain, growth failure/pubertal delay as a distinguishing pediatric feature of Crohn disease) and distinguish Crohn disease from ulcerative colitis by distribution and extraintestinal features.

entries.title: Cystic Fibrosis (GI/Pancreatic Manifestations)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/failure-to-thrive-infant-child/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: pancreatic-insufficiency malabsorption in CF is a classic cause of failure to thrive (objective 31-2).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/diarrhea/pediatric-diarrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: fat malabsorption from pancreatic insufficiency causes chronic steatorrheic diarrhea within objective 22-3's differential.

testable_competencies.gi_manifestations: Recognize CF's GI/pancreatic manifestations (meconium ileus in the newborn, pancreatic exocrine insufficiency causing steatorrhea and fat-soluble-vitamin deficiency, failure to thrive) and the role of newborn screening and sweat chloride testing in diagnosis.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps substantially with the Respirology section's 'Cystic Fibrosis' unit (P.S16.T03), which covers the pulmonary/CFTR-genetics/respiratory-management content in full; this GI-chapter unit is pancreatic/nutritional-manifestation focused. Both are independently full TN write-ups, not a duplicate cross-reference. Primary ownership not finalized at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/constipation/pediatric-constipation/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 16-2 'Pediatric constipation' is the paradigm objective for this unit.

testable_competencies.approach: Distinguish functional constipation (the overwhelming majority) from organic red flags (delayed meconium passage >48h suggesting Hirschsprung disease, ribbon stools, FTT) and outline first-line management (disimpaction, maintenance osmotic laxative, behavioural toileting strategies).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abdominal-pain/acute-abdominal-pain/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 3-2 (Acute abdominal pain) is the general parallel objective for identifying patients requiring emergency treatment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abdominal-pain/abdominal-pain-children/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 3-1 'Abdominal pain (children)' is the pediatric-specific paradigm objective for this unit.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Apply an age-stratified differential to acute pediatric abdominal pain (e.g. intussusception/malrotation in infants, appendicitis/mesenteric adenitis in older children) and recognize surgical-emergency red flags (peritoneal signs, bilious vomiting, hemodynamic instability).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abdominal-pain/chronic-abdominal-pain/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 3-3 (Chronic abdominal pain) is the paradigm objective, applicable to the pediatric functional-vs-organic differential (functional abdominal pain/IBS vs. celiac, IBD, constipation).

testable_competencies.approach: Distinguish functional chronic abdominal pain (normal growth, no alarm features) from organic causes (celiac disease, IBD, constipation) requiring targeted investigation.

entries.title: Pediatric Abdominal Mass

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/abdominal-masses-and-pelvic-masses/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 2 (Abdominal masses and pelvic masses) is the paradigm objective; the pediatric abdominal-mass differential (Wilms tumour, neuroblastoma, hepatoblastoma, intussusception) is an age-specific instance of this scope.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 115-1 (Acute visual disturbance / loss) applies directly -- orbital cellulitis is a sight- and life-threatening emergency (risk of cavernous sinus thrombosis) requiring urgent differentiation from the far more common, benign preseptal cellulitis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/sexual-dysfunctions-and-disorders/

testable_competencies.screening_and_counselling: Recognize the confidentiality and consent principles specific to adolescent STI screening/treatment, and outline the general approach to common STIs (chlamydia, gonorrhea, HPV) in an adolescent.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/sore-throat-and-or-rhinorrhea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 100 (Sore throat and/or rhinorrhea) covers upper-respiratory-complaint diagnosis; acute bacterial sinusitis is distinguished from prolonged viral URTI by persistence/severity/double-worsening pattern.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Distinguish acute bacterial sinusitis (persistent symptoms >10 d, severe onset, or double-worsening course) from a prolonged uncomplicated viral URTI.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: gestational-age/size classification (SGA/AGA/LGA, preterm/term/post-term) is foundational context for objective 64 (Neonatal distress) risk-stratification.

testable_competencies.routine_care: Outline routine newborn care after delivery (vitamin K administration, ocular antimicrobial prophylaxis, newborn metabolic/hearing screening, physical exam for congenital anomalies) and standard discharge criteria.

entries.title: Neonatal Resuscitation

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 64 'Neonatal distress' is the paradigm objective, explicitly requiring assessment of the need for and initiation of resuscitation in a distressed neonate.

testable_competencies.resuscitation_algorithm: Apply the neonatal resuscitation algorithm (initial steps -- warm, dry, stimulate, position airway; positive-pressure ventilation if apneic/HR<100; chest compressions and epinephrine if HR remains <60 despite adequate ventilation).

do_not_test: Exact current NRP algorithm timing intervals/compression ratios, which are periodically revised and must be verified source-first at question-generation stage rather than hard-coded now.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: apnea is a common presentation of neonatal distress (objective 64) in the preterm population, classified as central/obstructive/mixed.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish normal periodic breathing from pathologic apnea (>20 s, or shorter with bradycardia/desaturation), classify as central/obstructive/mixed, and recognize apnea of prematurity vs. apnea as a sign of underlying illness (sepsis, NEC) requiring sepsis workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/bleeding-bruising/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: neonate-specific bleeding-disorder causes (vitamin K deficiency, DIC from sepsis, thrombocytopenia) fall within objective 15-1's scope applied to the newborn period.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize neonatal bleeding-disorder causes (vitamin K deficiency, sepsis-associated DIC, maternal-antibody-mediated neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia) and distinguish from normal birth-trauma-related bruising.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pediatric-respiratory-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: BPD is a chronic-lung-disease-of-prematurity cause of objective 27-3 (Pediatric respiratory distress) in the former-preterm-infant population.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize BPD as chronic oxygen/ventilator-dependent lung disease of prematurity (defined by oxygen requirement at 36 wk corrected gestational age) and its long-term respiratory implications.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 19 'Cyanosis and hypoxia' is the paradigm objective; the hyperoxia test is the key bedside tool for distinguishing cardiac from pulmonary causes of neonatal cyanosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: neonatal cyanosis is a common presenting sign of objective 64's neonatal-distress scope.

testable_competencies.approach: Use the hyperoxia test and clinical context to distinguish cardiac (cyanotic CHD -- minimal PaO2 rise with 100% O2) from pulmonary/other causes (PaO2 rises substantially with 100% O2) of neonatal cyanosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct-component match: CDH is a classic cause of severe neonatal distress (objective 64) at birth (scaphoid abdomen, bowel sounds in the chest, pulmonary hypoplasia) requiring immediate airway management (avoid bag-mask ventilation, intubate) and surgical repair after stabilization.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_management: Recognize CDH by scaphoid abdomen and absent breath sounds with bowel sounds audible in the chest at birth, and the critical management point that bag-mask ventilation must be avoided (worsens bowel distension/lung compression) in favour of immediate intubation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypoglycemia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 129 'Hypoglycemia' is the paradigm objective, explicitly noting management should be prioritized and initiated even before a cause is identified -- directly applicable to at-risk neonates (infant of a diabetic mother, SGA/LGA, preterm).

testable_competencies.risk_and_management: Identify at-risk neonates for hypoglycemia (infant of a diabetic mother, SGA, LGA, preterm, perinatal stress) and initiate management (early feeding, IV dextrose for symptomatic or severe hypoglycemia) without delay for cause-finding.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-jaundice/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 49-1 'Neonatal jaundice' is the paradigm objective for this unit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/jaundice/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 49 (Jaundice, general) is the parent objective this pediatric-specific sub-objective specializes.

testable_competencies.approach: Distinguish physiologic jaundice (appears after 24h, peaks day 3-5, resolves by 2 wk) from pathologic jaundice (appears <24h, rapidly rising, or persisting >2-3 wk) requiring bilirubin-level-based phototherapy/exchange-transfusion decision-making, and recognize kernicterus as the feared complication of untreated severe hyperbilirubinemia.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct-component match: NEC is a classic preterm-neonate surgical emergency within objective 64's scope (feeding intolerance, abdominal distension, bloody stools, pneumatosis intestinalis on X-ray) requiring bowel rest and possible surgical intervention for perforation.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_management: Recognize NEC (preterm infant with feeding intolerance, abdominal distension, bloody stools, pneumatosis intestinalis or portal venous gas on abdominal X-ray) and initial management (bowel rest, broad-spectrum antibiotics, surgical consultation for perforation/pneumoperitoneum).

entries.title: Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: PPHN is a cause of severe neonatal cyanosis/hypoxemia (objective 19) refractory to oxygen, from failure of the normal postnatal drop in pulmonary vascular resistance.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize PPHN (severe hypoxemia out of proportion to CXR findings, differential pre-/post-ductal saturations, echo showing elevated pulmonary pressures without structural CHD) as a cause of refractory neonatal cyanosis.

entries.title: Respiratory Distress in the Newborn (RDS, TTN, Meconium Aspiration)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pediatric-respiratory-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 27-3 'Pediatric respiratory distress' is the paradigm objective, applicable to the newborn-specific differential (surfactant-deficiency RDS in preterm infants, transient tachypnea of the newborn after C-section/rapid delivery, meconium aspiration syndrome in post-term/distressed deliveries).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: respiratory distress is a leading presentation of objective 64's neonatal-distress scope.

testable_competencies.differential: Differentiate RDS (preterm, surfactant deficiency, ground-glass CXR, responds to surfactant/CPAP), transient tachypnea of the newborn (term/near-term, C-section or rapid delivery, self-limited retained-fetal-lung-fluid), and meconium aspiration syndrome (post-term, meconium-stained fluid, patchy infiltrates, risk of PPHN).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/visual-disturbance-loss/acute-visual-disturbance-loss/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 115-1 (Acute visual disturbance / loss) applies to ROP's vision-threatening potential; ROP is a screening-based condition in preterm/low-birth-weight infants exposed to supplemental oxygen.

testable_competencies.screening: Recognize preterm/low-birth-weight infants (especially with supplemental oxygen exposure) as requiring ROP screening given its potential for retinal detachment and vision loss if untreated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/neonatal-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct-component match: neonatal sepsis is a paradigm cause of objective 64's neonatal-distress scope, with nonspecific presentation (temperature instability, poor feeding, lethargy, respiratory distress) requiring a low threshold for full septic workup and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/temperature-abnormal-fever-and-or-chills/fever-and-hyperthermia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: fever (or hypothermia) in a neonate is a red-flag presentation within objective 107-1's scope warranting urgent sepsis evaluation.

testable_competencies.risk_and_management: Recognize early-onset (GBS, E. coli, vertical transmission) vs. late-onset (nosocomial, CoNS) neonatal sepsis risk factors and the nonspecific presentation, and initiate a full septic workup (blood/urine/CSF culture) with empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics given the low threshold for treatment in this population.

entries.title: Skin Conditions of the Neonate (Benign Findings, Differential)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/skin-and-integument-conditions/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 38 (Skin and integument conditions) covers determining whether a skin finding is benign; the classic benign neonatal skin findings (erythema toxicum, milia, Mongolian spots, transient neonatal pustular melanosis) are a specific instance requiring reassurance rather than workup.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Recognize common benign, self-resolving neonatal skin findings (erythema toxicum, milia, Mongolian spots) and distinguish them from findings warranting further evaluation.

entries.title: Approach to Common Pediatric Renal Diseases

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/renal-failure/acute-kidney-injury-anuria-or-oliguria/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 89-1 (Acute kidney injury) is the closest general-nephrology parallel objective this overview unit's approach content maps to.

testable_competencies.approach: Use an anatomic (glomerular vs. tubulointerstitial vs. obstructive) framework to approach a child with an abnormal urinalysis or renal-function abnormality.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/renal-failure/acute-kidney-injury-anuria-or-oliguria/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 89-1 (Acute kidney injury) applies directly -- HUS (typically post-diarrheal, Shiga-toxin-producing E. coli) is a paradigm pediatric AKI cause, presenting with the triad of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and AKI.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize HUS by its triad (microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury) typically following Shiga-toxin-producing E. coli (e.g. O157:H7) gastroenteritis, and that antibiotic treatment of the preceding diarrheal illness may increase HUS risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hematuria/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 8 (Hematuria) is the paradigm objective for nephritic syndrome's core presenting sign (gross/microscopic hematuria with red cell casts).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypertension/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: hypertension (objective 9-1) is a core feature of the nephritic-syndrome presentation alongside hematuria and edema.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize nephritic syndrome (hematuria with red cell casts, hypertension, oliguria, mild proteinuria) and the classic pediatric cause (post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, typically 1-2 wk after streptococcal pharyngitis or skin infection).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/proteinuria/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 84 (Proteinuria) is the paradigm objective for nephrotic syndrome's core presenting sign (heavy proteinuria).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/edema-anasarca-ascites/generalized-edema/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 29-1 (Generalized edema) applies directly to nephrotic syndrome's hypoalbuminemia-driven edema.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_management: Recognize nephrotic syndrome's tetrad (heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, hyperlipidemia) and that minimal change disease is the predominant pediatric cause, typically corticosteroid-responsive; recognize infection and thrombosis as key complications from urinary immunoglobulin/antithrombin loss.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypertension/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 9-1 'Hypertension' is the paradigm objective; pediatric hypertension is disproportionately secondary (renal, cardiovascular/coarctation, endocrine) compared to adult primary hypertension, a key age-specific teaching point.

testable_competencies.approach: Use age-/sex-/height-specific blood pressure percentiles to diagnose pediatric hypertension, and recognize that a secondary cause (renal parenchymal/renovascular disease, coarctation, endocrine) is more likely the younger the child and the more severe the hypertension.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/developmental-delay/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: CP is a leading cause of motor-domain developmental delay within objective 21's scope, though CP itself (a static encephalopathy) has no dedicated MCC objective.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cerebral palsy (non-progressive motor disorder from an early static brain insult, classified by motor type -- spastic/dyskinetic/ataxic -- and topographic distribution) and its common comorbidities (intellectual disability, seizures, feeding difficulty) requiring interdisciplinary management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/seizures-epilepsy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 92 'Seizures / epilepsy' is the paradigm objective, directly applicable to distinguishing simple from complex febrile seizures and their benign prognosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/temperature-abnormal-fever-and-or-chills/fever-and-hyperthermia/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: fever (objective 107-1) is the defining trigger and the febrile source should still be sought/treated.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Distinguish simple febrile seizure (generalized, <15 min, no recurrence in 24h, normal neuro exam, benign prognosis, no routine EEG/neuroimaging needed) from complex febrile seizure (focal, prolonged, or recurrent) warranting further workup.

entries.title: Hypotonic Infant

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypotonic-infant/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 71-2 'Hypotonic infant' is the paradigm objective for this unit.

testable_competencies.approach: Localize hypotonia as central (encephalopathic, more common: preserved strength, associated dysmorphism/seizures/altered alertness) vs. peripheral (motor unit disease: weakness prominent, areflexia, tongue fasciculations) using history and exam.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with the Development section's Motor Delay unit (P.S06.T08); primary ownership not finalized at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/congenital-anomalies-dysmorphic-features/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 36-2 (Congenital anomalies, dysmorphic features) covers recognizing a syndromic diagnosis from a constellation of physical findings, directly applicable to the NF1 diagnostic-criteria (>=2 of: cafe-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, optic glioma, axillary/inguinal freckling, distinctive bony lesion, affected first-degree relative).

testable_competencies.diagnostic_criteria: Apply NF1 diagnostic criteria (2 or more of: >6 cafe-au-lait spots, 2+ neurofibromas or 1 plexiform neurofibroma, 2+ Lisch nodules, optic glioma, axillary/inguinal freckling, a distinctive bony lesion, or an affected first-degree relative) and recognize associated learning disorders/seizures.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/congenital-anomalies-dysmorphic-features/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 36-2 (Congenital anomalies, dysmorphic features) covers syndromic diagnosis; NF2's diagnostic criteria (bilateral vestibular schwannomas, or a first-degree relative with NF2 plus specific tumour findings) are a specific instance.

testable_competencies.diagnostic_criteria: Recognize NF2's predisposition to intracranial/spinal tumours and its diagnostic criteria centred on bilateral vestibular schwannomas, distinguishing it from NF1.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/headache/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 39 'Headache' is the paradigm objective, requiring differentiation of benign (tension, migraine) from serious secondary causes -- directly applicable to this unit's primary-vs-secondary pediatric headache differential.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Differentiate primary headache (tension, migraine, cluster) from secondary causes requiring urgent workup (raised ICP from a mass lesion, meningitis) using red flags (early-morning headache/vomiting, focal neuro deficits, papilledema, worsening pattern).

entries.title: Approach to Pediatric Seizures (General Management, Seizure Mimics)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/seizures-epilepsy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 92 'Seizures / epilepsy' is the paradigm objective, explicitly requiring differentiation of a seizure from non-seizure conditions -- directly matching this unit's seizure-mimics content (breath-holding, syncope, pseudoseizure, TIA, tic) and general investigation/treatment-initiation approach.

testable_competencies.approach: Work up a first unprovoked seizure (electrolytes, glucose, EEG, neuroimaging if indicated) while excluding seizure mimics (breath-holding spells, syncope, night terrors, non-epileptic/pseudoseizure, TIA, tics), and apply general antiepileptic-therapy initiation principles (treat after 2+ unprovoked afebrile seizures, single-drug optimization before combination therapy).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/seizures-epilepsy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: infantile spasms/West syndrome is explicitly flagged in the source as a pediatric emergency requiring early identification given developmental-regression risk, a paradigm high-stakes teaching case for objective 92.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_urgency: Recognize infantile spasms (brief symmetric flexion/extension contractions in clusters, onset 4-8 mo, hypsarrhythmia on EEG) as a pediatric emergency requiring urgent identification and treatment to minimize developmental-regression risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/seizures-epilepsy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: a specific, lower-yield drug-resistant pediatric epilepsy syndrome within objective 92's differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Lennox-Gastaut syndrome's triad (multiple drug-resistant seizure types, cognitive/behavioural impairment, slow generalized spike-wave EEG) and its typically poor prognosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/seizures-epilepsy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: JME is a classic, high-yield adolescent-onset epilepsy syndrome (morning myoclonus, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, autosomal dominant with variable penetrance, excellent prognosis with lifelong valproic acid) within objective 92's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize JME (morning myoclonic jerks, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, adolescent onset, 3.5-6 Hz spike-wave EEG increased with photic stimulation) and that it requires lifelong antiepileptic therapy despite an otherwise excellent prognosis.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/seizures-epilepsy/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: childhood absence epilepsy (brief staring spells with 3 Hz spike-wave EEG, school-age onset) is a classic, high-yield pediatric epilepsy syndrome within objective 92's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize childhood absence epilepsy (brief staring/behavioural-arrest spells without postictal confusion, provoked by hyperventilation, classic 3 Hz generalized spike-and-wave EEG) and its generally good prognosis.

entries.title: Pediatric Asthma

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pediatric-respiratory-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 27-3 'Pediatric respiratory distress' is the paradigm objective for acute asthma exacerbation, and asthma is a major chronic cause of pediatric dyspnea (objective 27).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dyspnea/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 27 (Dyspnea) applies to the chronic-asthma-control dimension of this unit.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Diagnose pediatric asthma from recurrent wheeze/cough/dyspnea with reversibility, stratify severity/control, and outline a stepwise pharmacologic approach (SABA reliever, inhaled corticosteroid controller, add-on therapy), and recognize indications for hospitalization in an acute exacerbation.

do_not_test: Exact current step-wise asthma medication doses and specific guideline algorithm details, which are periodically revised and must be verified source-first at question-generation stage rather than hard-coded now.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pediatric-respiratory-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 27-3 'Pediatric respiratory distress' is the paradigm objective; bronchiolitis (usually RSV, <2 yr) is the classic infantile lower-respiratory-tract-infection cause of wheeze/respiratory distress.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Diagnose bronchiolitis clinically (viral URI prodrome progressing to wheeze/crackles/respiratory distress in a child <2 yr) and recognize that management is primarily supportive (no evidence benefit for bronchodilators/corticosteroids in typical cases), with palivizumab prophylaxis reserved for defined high-risk infants.

entries.title: Pneumonia (Pediatric, Respirology Chapter -- Age-Stratified Treatment)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pediatric-respiratory-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 27-3 'Pediatric respiratory distress' applies directly, with attention to interpreting respiratory rate relative to age -- the core teaching point of this unit's age-stratified pneumonia treatment table.

testable_competencies.age_stratified_management: Select first-line antibiotic therapy for community-acquired pneumonia based on the age-stratified table (e.g. ampicillin+gentamicin in neonates; high-dose amoxicillin in preschool/school-age children; azithromycin when atypical organisms are suspected in school-age children) and interpret respiratory rate relative to age when assessing severity.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps with the Infectious Diseases section's 'Pneumonia' unit (P.S12.T12); primary ownership not finalized at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pediatric-respiratory-distress/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 27-3 'Pediatric respiratory distress' is the paradigm objective for this unit's structured approach (sick-vs-not-sick assessment, upper vs. lower airway localization, age-appropriate investigations).

testable_competencies.approach: Apply the ABC-first, sick-vs-not-sick framework and an upper-airway (foreign body, croup) vs. lower-airway (bronchiolitis, pneumonia, asthma) localization approach to a child presenting with respiratory distress.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 50-3 'Nonarticular musculoskeletal pain' is the paradigm objective; growing pains is the classic benign diagnosis-of-exclusion cause (age 2-12 yr, intermittent, non-articular, typically evening/night bilateral leg pain, normal exam).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/pain/generalized-pain-disorders/

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose growing pains as a diagnosis of exclusion (bilateral lower-extremity pain, typically evening/nighttime, normal exam, no morning stiffness/limp/swelling) and recognize red flags that argue against it (unilateral pain, joint swelling, systemic symptoms, morning stiffness).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/joint-pain/polyarthralgia-pain-in-more-than-four-joints/

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/joint-pain/non-articular-musculoskeletal-pain/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 50-3 'Nonarticular musculoskeletal pain' is the paradigm objective for this unit's approach to limb pain not localized to a joint.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Apply an age-stratified differential to pediatric limb pain (trauma, growing pains, infection -- osteomyelitis, malignancy -- bone tumour/leukemia) and recognize red flags (night pain waking the child, systemic symptoms, focal bony tenderness) requiring urgent workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/limp-in-children/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 20 'Limp in children' is the paradigm objective, explicitly requiring ruling out the most serious (usually unilateral) diagnoses.

testable_competencies.approach: Apply an age-stratified differential to the limping child (developmental dysplasia of the hip and toddler's fracture in the young child; transient synovitis and Legg-Calve-Perthes in the young school-age child; SCFE in the adolescent) and recognize septic arthritis as the diagnosis that must never be missed.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/joint-pain/oligoarthralgia-pain-in-one-to-four-joints/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: Lyme arthritis is a large-joint (classically knee) monoarthritis cause within objective 50-1's oligoarthralgia differential, with a preceding erythema migrans history in an endemic area.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Lyme arthritis (large-joint monoarthritis, classically the knee, in a child with tick exposure in an endemic area +/- preceding erythema migrans) and the role of serologic testing and antibiotic treatment.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/joint-pain/oligoarthralgia-pain-in-one-to-four-joints/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: post-infectious reactive arthritis is a cause within objective 50-1's oligoarthralgia differential, typically following a GI or GU infection.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize reactive arthritis as a post-infectious (GI or GU pathogen) asymmetric oligoarthritis, distinguishing it from septic arthritis by the absence of active joint infection.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/limp-in-children/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: septic arthritis is the must-not-miss diagnosis within objective 20's limping-child differential, requiring urgent joint aspiration and IV antibiotics +/- surgical drainage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/trauma/bone-or-joint-injury/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: objective 109-3 (Bone or joint injury) covers the diagnostic approach to a painful joint/bone that osteomyelitis and septic arthritis fall under.

testable_competencies.red_flags_and_management: Recognize septic arthritis (Kocher criteria: fever, non-weight-bearing, elevated ESR/CRP, elevated WBC) as a surgical emergency requiring urgent joint aspiration and empiric IV antibiotics, and distinguish it from osteomyelitis (bony tenderness without joint effusion) and from transient synovitis (well-appearing, normal/mildly elevated inflammatory markers).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/joint-pain/polyarthralgia-pain-in-more-than-four-joints/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: SLE-associated polyarthralgia falls within objective 50-2's scope, though SLE itself (a multisystem autoimmune disease) has no single dedicated MCC presentation objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/skin-and-integument-conditions/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Weak/indirect match: the malar rash is a skin finding within objective 38's scope but is a secondary rather than primary teaching link for this unit.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pediatric SLE's multisystem presentation (malar rash, photosensitivity, arthritis, nephritis, cytopenias, positive ANA) and that pediatric-onset SLE tends to be more severe than adult-onset disease.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/limp-in-children/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: transient synovitis is the most common cause of an acutely limping/hip-pain-presenting young child within objective 20's scope, and its clinical distinction from septic arthritis (Kocher criteria) is a paradigm high-yield teaching point.

testable_competencies.differentiation: Distinguish transient synovitis (well-appearing, low-grade or no fever, able to bear some weight, normal/mildly elevated inflammatory markers, self-limited) from septic arthritis using the Kocher criteria.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: Kawasaki disease presents with prolonged fever (objective 107-1) as a cardinal criterion, alongside the other principal clinical criteria (conjunctivitis, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, mucositis, extremity changes).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/bleeding-bruising/
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: HSP's palpable purpura falls within objective 15-1's bleeding/bruising-appearing-lesion scope, though HSP is a vasculitis (normal platelet count) rather than a true bleeding disorder.

testable_competencies.recognition_and_urgency: Recognize Kawasaki disease's principal clinical criteria (fever >=5 d plus conjunctivitis, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, mucositis, extremity changes) and the urgency of IVIG treatment within 10 d of fever onset to prevent coronary artery aneurysm; recognize Henoch-Schonlein purpura's tetrad (palpable purpura, arthritis, abdominal pain, renal involvement) with a normal platelet count distinguishing it from ITP.
